newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL rubber closes higher in slow dealing.
newsitem.headline: KL rubber closes higher in slow dealing.

text.p: The Malaysian rubber market ended higher on local covering in slow trading due to players' reluctance to commit themselves heavily because of currency uncertainty, dealers said.

"The market has been quiet throughout the day. There were little price changes and buyers were keeping to the sidelines," a dealer at a trading firm said, expecting prices to hover around current levels.
"The main factor in the market is currency. We are still not confident about the regional currencies and don't want to take any risk," the dealer said.
Demand remains thin with Far East consumers seen checking on prices, dealers said. Most European buyers are out of the market because of the summer holidays.
Dealers offered SMR CV at 294 cents, SMR L at 275, SMR 5 at 254, SMR 10 at 248 and SMR 20 at 246 and latex at 190
At the close, both August RSS1 buyer and SMR 20 buyer ended half a cent higher at 249 cents (95 U.S. cents) and 248 cents a kg respectively.
The near-term prospects would depend on supply/demand situation and the weather conditions , dealers said.
